about: Markets Mint knows by name. Prices come from Yahoo's public chart feed by this symbol; anything else can be imported as a CSV. cls picks the cost and leverage class in venues.json, kind picks which venues can trade it, spread_pct overrides a venue's class spread for this one market. dividend_yield_pct (price indexes only) is the yearly dividend adjustment a CFD long is credited and a short pays. base (currency pairs only) is the currency a long holds; the pair's overnight funding is on the gap between the two currencies' rates. exchange_suffixes lists the exchanges (Yahoo's suffix: AX for the ASX, L for London) a share or fund missing from this list may come from; no suffix is a US listing. Shanghai, Shenzhen and Tel Aviv are left out on purpose: their index codes look like share codes (000001.SS, TA35.TA).

symbols.name: Vanguard Australian Shares ETF
symbols.blurb: About 300 of the biggest Australian companies in one fund. The plain benchmark for Australian money.

symbols.name: Betashares Australia 200 ETF
symbols.blurb: The 200 biggest Australian companies, one of the cheapest funds on the ASX.

symbols.name: SPDR S&P/ASX 200 Fund
symbols.blurb: The oldest ASX 200 fund (2001). Yahoo's prices start in January 2008, so a backtest on it includes the 2008 crash (about -51% to March 2009). Two pairs of one-day moves near 10% in August and September 2009 look like bad prints that cancel out.

symbols.name: Vanguard MSCI International Shares ETF
symbols.blurb: About 1,300 big companies outside Australia, priced in Australian dollars.

symbols.name: iShares S&P 500 ETF (ASX)
symbols.blurb: The 500 biggest US companies, bought on the ASX in Australian dollars.

symbols.name: Betashares NASDAQ 100 ETF
symbols.blurb: The 100 biggest non-financial NASDAQ companies: tech heavy, bigger swings.

symbols.name: Betashares Diversified All Growth ETF
symbols.blurb: Thousands of companies, Australian and worldwide, in one fund. Started 2019.

symbols.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
symbols.blurb: 90% shares, 10% bonds, Australian and worldwide, in one fund. Started 2017.

symbols.name: S&P/ASX 200 index (Australia 200 CFD)
symbols.blurb: The index itself: you can only trade it as a CFD. A long is credited the dividends (about 4.0% a year, measured from VAS.AX and STW.AX over 10 to 15 years), a short pays them; franking credits are not passed on.

symbols.name: S&P 500 index (US 500 CFD)
symbols.blurb: The 500 biggest US companies as a CFD, priced in US dollars. Dividend adjustment about 1.5% a year (measured from IVV.AX over 10 to 15 years).

symbols.name: NASDAQ-100 index (US-Tech 100 CFD)
symbols.blurb: US tech giants as a CFD, in US dollars. Dividend adjustment 0.8% a year, an assumption (NDQ.AX's 2.1% includes capital-gains payouts).

symbols.name: AUD/USD exchange rate
symbols.blurb: US dollars per Australian dollar. The most traded pair for Australians.

symbols.name: Gold (front-month futures)
symbols.blurb: Gold in US dollars an ounce. Futures prices jump a little at each monthly roll.

symbols.name: Crude oil WTI (front-month futures)
symbols.blurb: US oil in dollars a barrel. Wild swings, and a jump at every monthly roll.

symbols.name: Bitcoin in Australian dollars
symbols.blurb: Trades every day of the week. Has fallen more than 75% from a peak more than once.

symbols.name: BHP Group
symbols.warning: Picked because it is big today: a company that went bust would not be on this list, so a backtest on a single share flatters the idea (survivor bias).

symbols.name: Commonwealth Bank
symbols.warning: Picked because it is big today: a company that went bust would not be on this list, so a backtest on a single share flatters the idea (survivor bias).

symbols.name: Apple
symbols.warning: Picked because it is a winner today: hindsight. A backtest on one famous share says little about the next ten years (survivor bias).

symbols.name: Nvidia
symbols.warning: Picked because it is the biggest winner of recent years: pure hindsight. Do not read its backtest as a forecast (survivor bias).
